title: The kernels of a coherent formal system form a finite graded Rees module
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] with quasi-compact underlying space), let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, and let $(\mathcal F_n)_{n\ge1}$ be an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Set $\mathcal F_0=0$ and $\mathcal K_n=\operatorname{Ker}(\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n)$ in sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], for $n\ge0$ (thus $\mathcal K_0=\mathcal F_1$). Put $\mathcal I^0=\mathcal O_X$, with the other powers and quotients as in [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. The sheaf direct sum $\mathcal B=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal I^n/\mathcal I^{n+1}$ has its associated graded algebra structure: the homogeneous product is induced by multiplication of local sections, taking degrees $m,n$ to $m+n$, and its unit is $1\bmod\mathcal I$ in degree zero. Then $\mathcal G=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal K_n$ has a canonical graded $\mathcal B$-module structure, with degree-$m$ sections of $\mathcal B$ carrying $\mathcal K_n$ into $\mathcal K_{n+m}$, and its underlying $\mathcal O_X$-module is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. It is of finite type over $\mathcal B$: every point has an open neighbourhood $U$ and finitely many homogeneous sections of $\mathcal G|_U$ whose $\mathcal B|_U$-linear combinations locally generate all sections (equivalently there is a surjection from a finite direct sum of grading shifts of $\mathcal B|_U$ onto $\mathcal G|_U$). In fact these generators may be taken in degree zero. The action is specified locally by lifting $x\in\mathcal K_n$ to a section $\widetilde x$ of $\mathcal F_{n+m+1}$ and sending $(a\bmod\mathcal I^{m+1},x)$ to $a\widetilde x\in\mathcal K_{n+m}$, for $a\in\mathcal I^m$; lifts are taken after passing to a neighbourhood if necessary.

proof.text: *Construct the action.* Repeatedly applying the reduction condition of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] gives $\mathcal F_l/\mathcal I^r\mathcal F_l\cong\mathcal F_r$ for $l\ge r\ge1$: induction on $l-r$, using $\mathcal I^{l-1}\mathcal F_l\subseteq\mathcal I^r\mathcal F_l$ and the third isomorphism theorem for quotients. All transition maps are surjective as maps of sheaves. For $x\in\mathcal K_n$ and $a\in\mathcal I^m$, lift $x$ locally to $\widetilde x\in\mathcal F_{n+m+1}$. If $n\ge1$, its image in $\mathcal F_n$ is zero, so $\widetilde x\in\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_{n+m+1}$; for $n=0$ the same inclusion holds with $\mathcal I^0=\mathcal O_X$. Thus $a\widetilde x$ lies in $\mathcal I^{n+m}\mathcal F_{n+m+1}=\mathcal K_{n+m}$. A different lift differs by $\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F_{n+m+1}$, and multiplication by $a$ kills this difference since $\mathcal I^{n+m+1}\mathcal F_{n+m+1}=0$. Replacing $a$ by a section differing by $\mathcal I^{m+1}$ likewise changes the product by zero. These local choices agree on overlaps, so glue to bilinear action maps. Additivity, the unit law and associativity are verified with lifts to a single common level $\mathcal F_{n+m+l+1}$: for degrees $m,l$ both parenthesizations send the representative to $(ab)\widetilde x=a(b\widetilde x)$. The same multiplication calculation defines the associative unital algebra $\mathcal B$. Extending over the sheaf direct sums yields the claimed graded action.

proof.text: *Affine identification.* Work on an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $I=\mathcal I(U)$. The restriction is an object of $\mathit{Coh}(U,\widetilde I)$, since coherence and the reduction conditions are local. By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] (1), $M=\varprojlim_r\mathcal F_r(U)$ is finite over $\widehat A$ and the projections identify $\mathcal F_r(U)=M/I^rM$, compatibly with transitions. The kernel in degree $n$ is consequently $I^nM/I^{n+1}M$, also for $n=0$ because $\mathcal F_0=0$. Each $\mathcal K_n$ is quasi-coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel]. Affine sections of ideal products and quotients [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] identify the degree-$n$ part of $\mathcal B|_U$ with the associated sheaf of $I^n/I^{n+1}$. The counit and preservation of all colimits in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (3),(4) identify both sheaf direct sums with the associated sheaves of $B=\bigoplus I^n/I^{n+1}$ and $G=\bigoplus I^nM/I^{n+1}M$ respectively. In these identifications the action of step 1 is $(a,\bar x)\mapsto\overline{ax}$: a representative in $M$ supplies every lift used there. Thus the identifications respect multiplication and grading. In particular $\mathcal G|_U$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections].

proof.text: *Finite generation on the affine open.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-module-associated-graded-generators] to $A,I,M$. Choose a finite generating family of $M/IM$. The lemma says that it generates $G$ in degree zero over $B$, so gives a surjective $B$-linear graded map $B^{\oplus t}\to G$. It is also $A$-linear. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (4), associated sheaves preserve its cokernel and hence its surjectivity. Step 2 identifies the resulting morphism with a surjection $(\mathcal B|_U)^{\oplus t}\to\mathcal G|_U$ respecting the graded action. This proves finite type over $\mathcal B|_U$, without asserting finite type over $\mathcal O_U$.

proof.text: *Local conclusion.* Every point lies in an affine open $U$, where steps 2 and 3 establish quasi-coherence and provide finitely many degree-zero generators. Quasi-coherence and the stated finite-type condition are local, so these affine verifications give the conclusion on $X$. No global generating family or separation hypothesis on $X$ is required.

lean.statement: theorem formalSystems_kernel_rees_finite {X : Scheme.{ut}} [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData) (F : CoherentFormalModule X I) : (∐ (formalKernelPiece F)).IsQuasicoherent ∧ ∃ A : GradedSheafAlgebra (formalAssociatedGradedPiece I), A.unit = formalAssociatedGradedπ I 0 ∧ (∀ (m n : ℕ) (U : X.Opens) (a : (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι m).1.val.obj (op U)) (b : (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι n).1.val.obj (op U)), ∃ c : (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι (m + n)).1.val.obj (op U), (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι (m + n)).2.val.app (op U) c = (@id Γ(X, U) ((Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι m).2.val.app (op U) a)) * (@id Γ(X, U) ((Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι n).2.val.app (op U) b)) ∧ A.mul m n U ((formalAssociatedGradedπ I m).val.app (op U) a) ((formalAssociatedGradedπ I n).val.app (op U) b) = (formalAssociatedGradedπ I (m + n)).val.app (op U) c) ∧ ∃ M : GradedSheafModule A (formalKernelPiece F), M.IsLocallyGeneratedInDegreeZero ∧ ∀ (m n : ℕ) (U : X.Opens) (a : (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι m).1.val.obj (op U)) (x : (formalKernelPiece F n).val.obj (op U)) (t : (F.obj.obj (op (m + n))).val.obj (op U)), (F.obj.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_add_left n m)).op).val.app (op U) t = (formalKernelι F n).val.app (op U) x → (formalKernelι F (m + n)).val.app (op U) (M.act m n U ((formalAssociatedGradedπ I m).val.app (op U) a) x) = (@id Γ(X, U) ((Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι m).2.val.app (op U) a)) • t
